items: The defense team for Vice President Sara Duterte is focusing on allegations regarding P319 million in foreign remittances linked to Cale88 Foods Corporation, a company associated with her.

Witnesses, including legal and government officials, will testify to establish the legitimacy of Cale88 Foods, but experts express skepticism about the effectiveness of these testimonies in countering money laundering allegations.

The defense team of Vice President Sara Duterte appears to be shifting gears in the ongoing impeachment trial as they now seek to address one of the most contentious allegations against the second-highest official: the P319 million in foreign remittances allegedly received by Cale88 Foods Corporation, a company linked to her.

On Wednesday, November 18, Senate impeachment court spokesperson Reginald Tongol confirmed that the defense would present the following witnesses this week to address allegations surrounding the Duterte-linked company:

items: Lawyer Rainer Dela Fuente (AML Consulting PH) who would testify on fundamental legal concepts under the Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA), as amended
Dr. Ceferino S. Rodolfo, DTI undersecretary and BOI managing head, who would testify on Cale88 Foods Corporation’s registration with the Board of Investments (BOI)
Director Pilar Marilyn M. Pagayunan of FDA Center for Food Regulation and Research who would testify on Cale88’s FDA product registration for its sweetened banana chips

Rowena G. Mendoza, department manager of Center for International Expositions and Missions (CITEM), and/or a CITEM representative who would testify on DTI/CITEM communications and invitations sent to Cale88 Foods Corporation for food expositions

blocks.text: “All four are covered by requests for subpoena ad testificandum and duces tecum to controvert allegations under Article II,” Tongol said.
Cale88, a banana chips export company partly owned by Duterte’s husband, lawyer Mans Carpio, came under scrutiny in the ongoing impeachment trial over allegations of unexplained wealth.

Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura previously testified that Cale88 received P319 million in inward remittances from China and Hong Kong, based on covered transaction reports (CTRs) and suspicious transaction reports (STRs).

Lawyer Alex Cabrera, who prepared a financial forensic report on Duterte and Carpio’s wealth, described the company’s operations as a “revolving door,” which he said, was a “symptom of money laundering.”

“As for Cale88’s financial statements, many things are not in order. It has no payables or receivables. It is a manufacturer or exporter of manufactured goods, yet it has no inventory of raw materials or work in process, and no matter how much money comes in and goes out, it continues to incur losses,” Cabrera told the impeachment court. “That is not tinikling but a revolving door.”
Will the defense’s decision to present government officials and other experts to establish Cale88’s legitimacy as a registered food exporter be enough to counter allegations of money laundering?

To constitutional lawyer and law professor Lulu Reyes, establishing legitimacy will be helpful to the defense, but the witnesses will be a boost to their case “if they can definitely and directly testify on Cale88’s export transactions with its Chinese business partners.”
She added, “I doubt that they can.” If her doubts prove to be true, the defense will be hard-pressed to find more compelling witnesses.

Reyes further said the bank representatives whom the defense initially called to testify could have provided more relevant information about the transactions. But the defense backpedaled to expedite the proceedings supposedly. Could there have been other reasons?

“The best witnesses for the defense regarding Cale88 are the buyers or importers from China, customs brokers or freight companies who facilitate the trade, subcontractors or suppliers of Cale88 products, and of course, Cale88’s own employees with neat employment history in the company,” Reyes said.

Former senator Antonio Trillanes IV has accused Carpio of receiving P319 million in cash remittances from China through Cale88. The company is listed in the Vice President’s Statements of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALNs) from 2022 to 2025.
The defense began presenting its evidence last week as it sought to counter allegations of Duterte’s unexplained wealth under Article II of the Articles of Impeachment.

Among the witnesses presented were Davao City Assessor Jaime Adalin, who answered questions pertaining to allegations about Duterte’s undeclared properties in Davao, and lawyer Anel Martin Antero, who was presented to explain some of Carpio’s substantial credit card purchases previously flagged in Cabrera’s financial forensic report. The report alleged that Duterte and Carpio accumulated P817 million in unexplained wealth from 2022 to 2025. – Rappler.com
